Messages.Author: Sten During
Messages.Body:
The following occurred during a game.

Player A bleeds.

Player B blocks.

Stealth 1.

Intercept 1.

Stealth 2.

I tap London Evening Star Tabloid Newspaper for another intercept.

Player B protests as he wants to play Telepathic Misdirection in order
to
bounce the bleed to me.

Questions:

Did he have the right to refuse the extra intercept as he's the prey and
thus
gets to react before me?

If not, did he get the extra intercept because I tapped before he
announced
Telepathic Misdirection?

If not, did he get the extra intercept because all tapping is
'immediate'?

If not, did he get the extra intercept because I'm allowed to forcefully

prolong the process to determine wether the blocking attempt is
succesful or not, no matter if he had announced his bounce before I
tapped, ie anything prolonging the process to check if a block is
succesful will always be playable until that process is finally
resolved.

Sten During

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <3BDD43AA...@netg.se>, Sten During <ya...@netg.se>
writes:

>The following occurred during a game.
>Player A bleeds.
>Player B blocks.
>Stealth 1.
>Intercept 1.
>Stealth 2.
>I tap London Evening Star Tabloid Newspaper for another intercept.
>Player B protests as he wants to play Telepathic Misdirection in order
>to
>bounce the bleed to me.
>

>Did he have the right to refuse the extra intercept as he's the prey and
>thus
>gets to react before me?

Yes. [1.6.1.6]

"Sequencing: If two or more players want to play a card or effect, the
acting Methuselah plays first. At every stage, the acting player always
has the opportunity to play the next card or effect. So after playing
one effect, she may play another and another. Once she is finished, the
opportunity passes to the defending Methuselah (in the cases of directed
actions and combat), then to the rest of the Methuselahs in clockwise
order from the acting Methuselah. Note that if any card or effect is
used by any Methuselah, the acting Methuselah again gets the opportunity
to play the next effect."

>If not, did he get the extra intercept because I tapped before he
>announced
>Telepathic Misdirection?

If you had said "Do you want me to give you the intercept?" (or
similar), and they'd said "Yes", thus yielding their right to play at
that time, it would have gone first, yes.

>If not, did he get the extra intercept because all tapping is
>'immediate'?

All tapping is immediate, yes. But it doesn't just happen entirely
randomly.

>If not, did he get the extra intercept because I'm allowed to forcefully
>prolong the process to determine wether the blocking attempt is
>succesful or not

No. Each player has the right to play an effect in sequence.

Hmm, even though I realise what I'm suggesting below is not the case, then
what you state above would prevent me (being neither acting nor defending
Metuselah) from playing Direct Intervention on an action-modifier as long
as the acting Metuselah states that he/she still have more modifiers to play.

Also, is there no 'phase-handling' that eventually overrides the sequencing-
rules. For example, a hypothetical card that allows you to make a minion
you don't control maneouver in combat. If such a card doesn't state that
the minion can choose to accept such a maneouver or not (similar to the
intercept given by tapping London Evening Star - card doesn't give the
receiving minion any opportunity NOT to gain extra intercept), then
both combatants would still be locked in the determine range part of
the combat - albeit unvillingly.

The reason for this added question is that stealth/intercept -resolution
for blocking is described pretty much the same way as maneouver/
countermaneouver.

But card-canceling effects are played when another card (the card to be
canceled) is played. See more below.

> Also, is there no 'phase-handling' that eventually overrides the sequencing-
> rules.

Yes. You cannot rush through/past a phase to keep others from using effects in
that phase. So you can't (above) rush past the "card played" step to avoid
getting DI'ed.

> For example, a hypothetical card that allows you to make a minion
> you don't control maneouver in combat. If such a card doesn't state that

I don't understand the problem with that example.

Yeah - the block cannot succeed or fail until all the effects are in (unless
one of the effects makes the would-be blocker inelligible to block, of course,
which is where the Telepathic Misdirection play can come in - chaning the
target of the bleed will make the would-be blocker controlled by the former
target inelligible to block).

Incidentally:
There's a slight gray area at the moment of successful blocking.
I'll put that on the RT list for closer inspection to see if we can't resolve
the procedure to a finer level.

Messages.Author: Tobias Loehr
Messages.Body:
Sten During <ya...@netg.se> wrote in message news:<3BDD43AA...@netg.se>...

> The following occurred during a game.

>
> Stealth 2.

> to
> bounce the bleed to me.
>
> Questions:
>
> Did he have the right to refuse the extra intercept as he's the prey and
> thus
> gets to react before me?

Technically I believe you should have waited until he was done playing
cards and then actually asked you for help.

>
> If not, did he get the extra intercept because I tapped before he
> announced
> Telepathic Misdirection?

He still got the Intercept, but he does not have to block now. He can
still play that TM and you will be without you Newspaper

>
> If not, did he get the extra intercept because all tapping is
> 'immediate'?

The timing doesn't really matter in this case. You tapped the card
and he got the Intercept. That doesn't preclude or stop the playing
of any other cards (other than further intercept cards).

>
> If not, did he get the extra intercept because I'm allowed to forcefully
>
> prolong the process to determine wether the blocking attempt is
> succesful or not, no matter if he had announced his bounce before I
> tapped, ie anything prolonging the process to check if a block is
> succesful will always be playable until that process is finally
> resolved.
>
> Sten During

Whether the Intercept was enough or not, he can still play his bounce
card. He is truly under no obligation to actually block once it is
announced if he can get out of it (with a bounce).
